text: Add request-context categorical features (tab, hour, weekday) to the additive user/video-ID scorer.
rationale: This is the only feature family with a positive training-only temporal screen, full coverage, and positive primary movement on each of four holdout dates. It directly permits context-dependent within-user video ordering.
exact_ablation: Add exactly three train-vocabulary categorical fields—tab, hour derived from hourmin, and weekday derived from date—to the existing additive user_id/video_id model; leave optimizer, loss, epochs, and all other features unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 versus the unscored ID scaffold, from context-specific score shifts among a user's displayed videos.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.004; top-five benefit is expected to be similar but must be independently verified.

text: Add only tab as a categorical request-context feature to the additive ID scorer.
rationale: Tab is an impression-time request-context field within the sole prioritized feature family. This isolated ablation tests whether the broad context result is predominantly surface/context selection rather than time variation.
exact_ablation: Add only tab, with a train-fitted vocabulary and explicit unknown bucket, to the seed user_id/video_id feature matrix; do not add hour or weekday.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.002, likely smaller than the complete context family because it captures only one contextual axis.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.002, with risk of no movement if tab primarily changes calibration.

text: Add only hour-of-day as a categorical request-context feature to the additive ID scorer.
rationale: Hour is part of the temporally consistent request-context screen and is known at ranking time. Isolating it avoids conflating diurnal effects with tab and weekday effects.
exact_ablation: Add only hour derived from hourmin as a 24-value train-vocabulary categorical field to the seed user_id/video_id model; leave tab and weekday absent.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.002, if viewing preferences differ sufficiently by time of day within user.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.002, potentially weaker than GAUC because time effects may separate lower-ranked candidates too.

text: Add only weekday as a categorical request-context feature to the additive ID scorer.
rationale: Weekday is an available pre-impression temporal context field included in the only positive feature-family result. This low-cost ablation tests weekly preference variation independently.
exact_ablation: Add only weekday derived from date as a seven-category train-vocabulary field to the seed user_id/video_id model; do not add tab or hour.

expected_effect.GAUC: 0.000 to +0.001, as weekly effects are expected to be weaker than the complete context group.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: 0.000 to +0.001, with a substantial chance of being flat due to the coarse seven-category signal.

text: Replace additive ID weights with a factorization-machine interaction between user ID and video ID.
rationale: The seed contains user and video identifiers but only additive effects, which cannot express user-video affinity. A single low-rank interaction mechanism makes scores vary meaningfully among a user's candidate videos without introducing unapproved feature families.
exact_ablation: Replace the seed's additive linear user_id/video_id scoring function with a rank-32 factorization-machine interaction over the same two ID fields; retain pointwise BCE, split logic, and training schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.002 to +0.010, because personalized user-video interactions directly target within-user positive-negative ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.008, provided affinity interactions promote positives into the top five rather than only widening lower-rank margins.

text: Replace additive ID weights with user and video embeddings followed by a shallow MLP scorer.
rationale: A nonlinear scorer over learned user/video representations is a concrete way to model affinity beyond additive ID effects while retaining the seed's permissible fields only.
exact_ablation: Replace the additive two-ID linear model with 32-dimensional user and video embeddings concatenated into a single 64-to-32 ReLU MLP and scalar head; retain BCE and no additional features.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.008 through nonlinear personalized item ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.006; it may lag GAUC if additional capacity mostly improves margins outside the top five.

text: Use a Deep & Cross scorer over user ID, video ID, and the approved request-context fields.
rationale: The measured context-family gain suggests interactions between request context and identity may matter. A bounded cross branch is a single architecture ablation that can learn such conjunctions without adding screened-negative feature families.
exact_ablation: Replace the additive scorer with a two-layer low-rank Deep & Cross model whose only inputs are user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday; retain pointwise BCE and all split handling.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.002 to +0.007 if ID-by-context interactions improve within-user ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.006, with possible underperformance if rare ID-context combinations overfit.

text: Apply inverse per-user candidate-count weighting to the seed pointwise BCE.
rationale: Official GAUC aggregates within-user AUC with positive-count weighting, while unweighted row BCE can be dominated by prolific users. User-normalized loss is a clean objective-only alignment test using no new features.
exact_ablation: Keep the seed model and features unchanged, but weight each training-row BCE by the reciprocal of that user's training candidate count, computed only within the fixed training split.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.000 to +0.004 if prolific-user dominance currently distorts optimization.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.002; equal-user weighting may not emphasize top-five placement and can trade off top-rank quality.

text: Train the seed ID scorer with within-user RankNet pairwise loss instead of pointwise BCE.
rationale: GAUC is based on within-user positive-negative ordering, so a pairwise objective is directionally aligned with the official metric. This changes only the loss and retains allowed identifiers.
exact_ablation: Replace pointwise BCE with deterministic within-user positive-versus-negative RankNet loss on training rows, sampling up to four negatives per positive from the same user; keep the seed model and features unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.006 if training users provide enough mixed-label comparisons.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.001 to +0.004; pairwise ordering can improve GAUC without consistently correcting the very top five.

text: Add an L2-normalized user-video embedding dot-product scorer with no new features.
rationale: A normalized dot-product embedding model tests compact personalized affinity while constraining score growth and parameter memorization. It is materially distinct from additive IDs and MLP scoring.
exact_ablation: Replace the additive seed scoring function with the dot product of L2-normalized 32-dimensional user and video embeddings plus one global bias; retain BCE and all data handling.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.007 through direct personalized affinity ranking.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.005, but normalized capacity may be insufficient for users with multiple unrelated interests.

text: Add feature-cross embeddings for video ID by tab to the additive seed scorer.
rationale: The positive request-context evidence supports testing a single interpretable context interaction. Video-by-tab permits the same video to receive a different score on different request surfaces while avoiding rejected metadata and history fields.
exact_ablation: Add one hashed categorical interaction field formed as video_id concatenated with tab to the seed's existing additive feature matrix; do not add any other context field or model change.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 if video suitability differs by tab within user.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.001 to +0.003, with gains limited by sparse video-tab combinations.

text: Add feature-cross embeddings for user ID by hour to the additive seed scorer.
rationale: The positive context screen makes an interpretable user-by-time interaction plausible: individual users may have different time-of-day viewing preferences. This is a single feature-cross ablation using ranking-time fields only.
exact_ablation: Add one hashed categorical interaction field formed as user_id concatenated with hour derived from hourmin to the seed additive model; do not add tab, weekday, or other fields.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.001 to +0.004 if hour-specific user preferences reorder candidates.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.000 to +0.003; sparse user-hour cells may yield weaker top-five movement than GAUC movement.
